subject: dispatch_release

observation.summary: A bare-name match for the regex anchor 'dispatch_release$' on the arm64e slice yields zero lines. The arm64e binary does export _dispatch_release (offset 0x45E4) -- the internal leading-underscore form that the OSS public macro dispatch_release() in src/object.c:216 de-sugars to -- but no public-name dispatch_release symbol is in the arm64e export trie. This is consistent with the Swift/ARC migration of GCD ownership away from explicit dispatch_release, where modern clients compile dispatch_release calls to objc_release/_os_object_release and the legacy public symbol was deliberately retired from the export trie.

claim: The public function dispatch_release is ABSENT from the arm64e export trie of libdispatch (macOS 27). Only the underscored internal symbol _dispatch_release (offset 0x45E4 on arm64e) is exported. This absence is the canonical signature of the GCD-to-ARC ownership migration: the OSS public macro dispatch_release(dou) at src/object.c:216 is now compiled out at the call site (the dispatch/header makes it a no-op under -DOS_OBJECT_USE_OBJC) and the function-form symbol was therefore retired from the public export trie in shipped libdispatch. Tools or bindings that look up 'dispatch_release' directly from dlsym() will fail; the supported path is the underscored _dispatch_release, _os_object_release, or objc_release depending on the object kind.

cross_reference.label: object.c: public dispatch_release entry (OSS -- absent in shipped)
object.h: dispatch_release macro definition (no-op under ARC)

reproducer:
nm -arch arm64e -gU /usr/lib/system/introspection/libdispatch.dylib | grep -E '^[0-9a-fA-F]+ T dispatch_release$'
# expect zero output -- the public anchor is gone
nm -arch arm64e -gU /usr/lib/system/introspection/libdispatch.dylib | grep -E '_dispatch_release$'
# expect a single line: 0x000045E4 T _dispatch_release
